column1: zsh/bash: why does `/proc/$!/cmdline` give `event not found` interactively?
column2:
Interactive shells read `!` as history expansion (`!!`, `!vim`, `!42`) on the RAW line BEFORE variables expand, so a `!` inside a word is taken as a history event. Scripts and `sh -c` have it OFF (why the same line works there).

Fix: capture the PID immediately, then use the plain var (no `!` downstream):
  pid=$!
  tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/$pid/cmdline
Session off-switch: `setopt nobanghist` (zsh) / `set +H` (bash).

column1: Shell: why doesn't `man umask` work, and how do you get real docs for a builtin?
column2:
A builtin (umask, cd, export, read, setopt, hash) lives INSIDE the shell, so it has no standalone man page — `man umask` is a generic POSIX stub, not your shell's behavior.

Ask the shell instead:
  run-help umask     # zsh (autoload -Uz run-help; OMZ binds Esc-h)
  man zshbuiltins    # all zsh builtins (also: man zshall)
  help umask         # bash equivalent
  type umask         # -> 'umask is a shell builtin'

column1: Linux: what does `umask` do, and what perms result from `umask 077`?
column2:
umask = permission bits to REMOVE from the base when a file/dir is created (result = base & ~umask). Octal, per-process, inherited by children.

Base: files 666, dirs 777 (files get NO execute by default).
  umask 077 -> file 600 rw------- , dir 700 rwx------
  umask 022 -> file 644 rw-r--r-- , dir 755 rwxr-xr-x
It only REMOVES bits, never adds — `chmod +x` is still needed to make a file executable.

column1: zsh: startup files and load order — which runs for login / interactive / scripts?
column2:
"rc" = "run commands". zsh reads a SET, in order (system /etc/zsh/* just before each ~/.*):
  ~/.zshenv    ALWAYS — login, interactive, AND scripts   (keep TINY)
  ~/.zprofile  login only, before .zshrc
  ~/.zshrc     interactive — the main one (aliases, prompt, options)
  ~/.zlogin    login only, after .zshrc
  ~/.zlogout   login, on logout
By type: login -> zshenv,zprofile,zshrc,zlogin. Interactive -> zshenv,zshrc. Script -> zshenv only.
GOTCHA: .zshenv runs for scripts too — heavy work there slows every script.
